historical_metadata_policies.reason: This class vtable's canonical cartridge storage 0x02128bfc..0x02128c80 remains ROM-gap owned, outside this TU's owned .data 0x02128b38..0x02128bc8. The earlier text/init-only ownership description is historical: this manifest now also owns .ctor, .data and .bss. Extent corroborated three ways: the cartridge words put mwcc's two-word preamble {0x00000000, 0x02128bd4} at 0x02128bfc and the last slot at 0x02128c7c, with _ZTI15daObjIceBlock_c next at 0x02128c80, so the OBJECT is 0x02128bfc..0x02128c80 = 0x84 bytes; tools/rtti_vtables.py --own daGmch_c reports 31 slots (0x7c) plus the 0x8 preamble = 0x84; the emitted _ZTV8daGmch_c is 0x84. symbols.txt names the address point 0x02128c04, which is the convention romdata_check re-derives the object start from.
this class RTTI record (__si_class_type_info: {0x0209a764, 0x02128bc8, 0x0208e390}); the canonical cartridge copy remains ROM-gap owned.

this class RTTI name. The cartridge itself spells it "8daGmch_c" at 0x02128bc8, so this is a recovered name and not a coined one and the row really is compared against the ROM. That comparison is why the class had to be renamed out of the tree's coined `Moneybag` before promotion: BOTH names are 8 characters, so a Moneybag-named TU would have emitted a 10-byte _ZTS of exactly the right SIZE and the wrong CONTENT, which no size or extent check catches. The canonical cartridge copy remains ROM-gap owned.
